subject: Clarify indemnity attestation, evidence custody, and split responsibility
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@tremontbio.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement - Tremont Bio <procurement@tremontbio.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — indemnity evidence and attestation request

David / Grace,

Thanks again for walking us through the MSA redlines yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams asked for two concrete clarifications before we can push an order form through:

1) Attestation language: they want a short, signed attestation from Redwood that describes what types of artifacts you will preserve and provide if a third-party IP infringement claim arises from customer-generated prompts / model output (logs, prompt + model hash, timestamped token stream, and any cached KV data).

2) Evidence custody & timeline: the procurement team wants an explicit timeline for how quickly Redwood can produce a forensic package once a notice is received, and whether Redwood will custody originals or provide copies. They also flagged the need for clarity on who owns/retains the investigation artifacts for regulatory or litigation hold needs.

Attached is our consolidated redlines_v3.docx and an initial evidence checklist (evidence_checklist.xlsx) that shows what the customer expects to receive.

Finally, our legal ops team asked whether Redwood is open to a narrow carve for defense-control in cases where the alleged infringement is solely a result of a customer-supplied dataset (i.e., not model-generated content). They want to understand how Redwood would allocate defense control and cost in a mixed-origin claim.

Can you confirm these three items — attestation language, production timeline / custody approach, and proposed cost/defense split for mixed-origin claims — by EOD so procurement can escalate internally? If easier, we can jump on a 30-min call.

Best,
Sarah

Sarah Li
Sr. Legal Counsel, Tremont Bio
legalops@tremontbio.com

Attachments: redlines_v3.docx (docx), evidence_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@tremontbio.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — indemnity evidence and attestation request

Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Looping in Grace (ops), Ben (commercial), and Irene (legal) to get the right level of detail.

High level from Redwood: we will defend or reimburse for third-party IP claims tied to model output only when the customer provides timely notice and cooperation, and when the claim is demonstrably caused by output that reproduces third-party protected content. For your three asks below:

1) Attestation language — See Irene's proposed short attestation in her follow-up. It focuses on the artifacts we can reasonably produce (structured request / preservation scope) rather than a guarantee about third-party ownership. We prefer attestation that confirms Redwood will preserve and provide the forensic package described in the evidence checklist upon receipt of a valid claim notice.

2) Production timeline & custody — operationally we can assemble a forensic package within 10 business days for urgent incidents; for complex or cross-region matters it can be 15 business days. We generally provide copies of raw logs and a signed statement from our forensics team; Redwood does not transfer originals for production systems but can provide certified copies and a chain-of-custody affidavit where necessary. Grace, please flag anything operationally infeasible here.

3) Mixed-origin defense/ cost split — we are willing to propose a waterfall approach: (a) where the claim is solely caused by model-generated output, Redwood will assume defense (subject to our standard notice/cooperation terms); (b) where a claim is solely caused by customer-supplied content, the customer controls defense; (c) for mixed-origin claims we propose shared defense control with cost-splitting proportional to agreed attribution (or a default 50/50 split if attribution cannot be reasonably established). Irene will propose precise contract language for the order form.

If Tremont needs an executive exception to the defense-control requirement for a narrow use-case, Ben can follow up on commercial terms. Happy to take a quick call; otherwise we'll get back with redline text this afternoon.

Thanks,
David

David Kim
Head of Legal Partnerships | Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@tremontbio.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed attestation text and evidence checklist (redlines)

Sarah — attaching suggested contract text inline here for quick review, plus an operational checklist we are prepared to commit to in the order form. Happy to iterate.

Proposed short attestation (order-form paragraph):
"Redwood Inference will, upon timely written notice of a third-party claim alleging that Model Output infringes third-party intellectual property rights, preserve and provide to Customer a forensic evidence package consisting of (i) request metadata and timestamps, (ii) the prompt and immediate pre/post context, (iii) model identifier and version (including checkpoint hash), (iv) token stream and where feasible sequence offsets, (v) any cached KV data or prefix cache relevant to the request, and (vi) execution logs necessary to reproduce inference. Redwood will produce certified copies of these artifacts and reasonable chain-of-custody documentation within the timeline set forth in the Order Form. This attestation is limited to Redwood's operational ability to collect and produce such artifacts and does not constitute an opinion on ownership or validity of any third-party claims."

Operational evidence checklist (we propose to list in the order form appendix):
- Request ID(s) and timestamps (UTC)
- Prompt and immediate preceding context (as provided by customer)
- Model id, revision, and quantization profile
- Token stream log and generation probabilities (where retained)
- KV cache contents and whether prefix caching was in effect
- System logs (container id, node id) and inferencing job ids
- Redaction map and redaction justification (if any items were redacted)
- Chain-of-custody affidavit signed by Redwood forensics lead

Production timeline: Redwood to provide an initial certified package within 10 business days of receipt of materially complete notice. If additional data is required, Redwood will notify customer within that window and provide an expected supplemental delivery date.

Defense-control / cost-split language (suggestion for order form):
- "If the allegation is reasonably attributable solely to Model Output generated by Redwood models, Redwood will defend and control the defense subject to the Customer's right to participate. If the allegation is reasonably attributable solely to Customer-supplied content, Customer will defend and control the defense. For claims with both Customer content and Model Output involvement, the parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to agree on attribution and allocation of defense costs; absent agreement within 30 days, defense costs will be apportioned 50/50 between the parties, subject to rights to seek indemnity or contribution post-resolution."

We intentionally kept the attestation operational and limited liability/opinion statements out of the attestation itself. If Tremont requires different warranty-style language or a lower production timeline for certain regulated workflows, please highlight which uses and we can escalate for an executive exception.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachments: redlines_v3.docx (suggested text highlighted), evidence_checklist.xlsx (detailed fields)

Subject: Re: Proposed attestation text and evidence checklist (redlines)

Irene / David — thanks for the quick and detailed responses. The attestation text and checklist look reasonable and aligned with what our audit team needs. Two follow-ups before we mark this cleared for procurement: 

1) Timeline exception: we have one regulated program that needs evidence within 5 business days for incident triage. Would Redwood consider a contractual SLA here for that named program in the Order Form Appendix in exchange for a higher per-request fee or a limited carveout? If so, procurement will draft the appendix and Ben (cc'd) and I can discuss commercial terms.

2) Cost-split examples: the 50/50 fallback is workable as a default, but our counsel asked for a short example in the contract appendix to show how attribution would be determined operationally (e.g., token-level reproduction analysis + provenance scoring). Can Redwood commit to using a neutral third-party forensic lab for attribution if the parties cannot agree? If Redwood agrees, we will add a short escalation path in the order form.

If you can confirm these two items in writing, procurement will clear the order-form redlines and route for signatures. If it's easier, we can take a 20-min call tomorrow to tie these up.

Thanks — Sarah

Sarah Li
Sr. Legal Counsel, Tremont Bio
legalops@tremontbio.com
